components.functionality: Container-only OpenCodex bind configuration
components.incompatibility: OpenCodex has a configuration schema but no container bind configuration; a two-field instance is required so the unchanged server can listen outside its container namespace.

parityAudit.decision: This is deployment data consumed by the upstream loader and contains no replacement configuration logic.

components.functionality: Local composition of OpenCodex and Codex-Wrapper services
components.incompatibility: The upstream compose starts only Codex-Wrapper and cannot compose the independently imported OpenCodex management server, multi-auth state volume and AIWrapper profile adapter paths.

parityAudit.decision: Service composition is an allowed integration layer; each service continues running its upstream runtime rather than a replacement.

components.functionality: Deploy the built AIWrapper GUI into the static directory used by the unchanged OpenCodex server
components.incompatibility: OpenCodex serves only its package-local gui/dist and exposes no external GUI directory setting; modifying the preserved upstream snapshot would destroy traceability.

retained: Original OpenCodex static-file server and path contract
parityAudit.decision: Copy build artifacts at packaging time while leaving the upstream server unchanged.

components.functionality: Opt-in production smoke across browser authentication, model discovery, real SSE provider execution, conversation persistence, export, sharing and usage accounting
components.incompatibility: 9router's live E2E covers RTK at its own proxy and OpenCodex's runtime smoke covers an isolated provider process, but neither can authenticate an AIWrapper principal or inspect its session, share and governance domains. The live opt-in, direct fetch, bounded wait and server-contract architecture are reusable; the assertions must target the composed product boundary.

retained: Explicit opt-in before live provider traffic
Real HTTP proxy request instead of an in-process mock
lost: 9router log-file RTK assertion remains covered by the directly executed RTK integration test
OpenCodex isolated child restart proof remains in the complete imported upstream suite
parityAudit.decision: Adapt the mature live-smoke boundary to prove the composed AIWrapper product and add secret redaction plus deterministic cleanup; do not introduce a second browser automation stack.

components.functionality: Real Chrome discovery, CDP connection, renderer readiness, deterministic viewport and screenshot capture for production UI verification
components.incompatibility: None for the CDP transport helpers: AIWrapper imports and executes the original CommonJS module directly. Traycer's zoom-preference readers are not invoked because AIWrapper is a browser application rather than its Electron desktop shell.

parityAudit.decision: Execute the original Traycer CDP helpers from upstream and keep AIWrapper-specific assertions outside that module.

components.functionality: Fresh-profile Chrome journey through login, onboarding, role-aware navigation, streamed chat, session history, archive, disconnect and browser-error audit
components.incompatibility: Traycer's runner launches its Electron binary and verifies resolution/zoom persistence. AIWrapper is served by the unchanged OpenCodex HTTP runtime, so the launch target and product assertions differ; free-port allocation, throwaway profile, child lifecycle, CDP readiness, screenshot evidence and bounded cleanup remain portable.

parityAudit.decision: Preserve Traycer's live CDP harness architecture and replace only the Electron launch and resolution assertions with the composed OpenCodex/AIWrapper user journey.

components.functionality: Secret-safe and cache-efficient Docker build context for the composed upstream runtimes
components.incompatibility: The upstream ignore file assumes a single Python repository. AIWrapper's build context also contains Bun, Node, multiple complete upstream snapshots, generated provenance and local AIWrapper state, so the original rules alone would send credentials and large transient trees to the Docker daemon.

retained: Narrow retention of codex-multi-auth's original compiled vendor packages required by its frozen local-file dependencies
parityAudit.decision: Preserve the original denylist and extend it for the multi-runtime repository while explicitly retaining only public environment examples and codex-multi-auth's tracked vendor package artifacts.

components.functionality: Production composition of the original Codex-Wrapper and OpenCodex runtimes behind a private dependency-aware network
components.incompatibility: Codex-Wrapper's original Compose runs one service and publishes it directly. AIWrapper must compose the unchanged OpenCodex data plane, the extended Codex-Wrapper gateway and one public ingress, enforce dependency health, share the protected OAuth directory with asymmetric permissions and keep state durable.

lost: Direct publication of the backend port is intentionally removed from production
parityAudit.decision: Keep the original service contract and add only the OpenCodex dependency, AIWrapper integration environment, health ordering, durable state and same-origin ingress required by the composed product.

components.functionality: Single-origin Nginx ingress with OpenCodex shell routing, AIWrapper prefix isolation, security headers and unbuffered SSE
components.incompatibility: 9router documents separate dashboard and API ports on one application. AIWrapper has two preserved upstream runtimes with overlapping root API paths, so the API must be isolated under /aiwrapper while OpenCodex continues to own the root shell and provider data plane.

retained: Forwarded host, address and protocol headers
lost: Certificate termination remains the responsibility of the host proxy so the container can run behind any production TLS provider
parityAudit.decision: Adapt the original dual-route Nginx pattern to a same-origin /aiwrapper prefix and retain the complete streaming requirements.

components.functionality: Explicit production environment template for public origin, protected OAuth storage, secure cookies and independent data-plane, administration and owner secrets
components.incompatibility: 9router's environment contract configures one JWT-protected application. AIWrapper needs independent OpenCodex data-plane, OpenCodex administration and AIWrapper owner secrets, the shared Codex OAuth path, a canonical browser origin and explicit secure-cookie and ingress binding controls.

retained: Requirement to replace all credential placeholders
lost: 9router-specific JWT and initial-password variables do not exist in the imported runtimes
parityAudit.decision: Keep the explicit upstream production-secret contract and map it to the real authentication and topology boundaries of AIWrapper.

components.functionality: Stable independent OpenCodex management credential across container replacement with anonymous rejection and authenticated verification
components.incompatibility: OpenCodex can atomically create an administrator token file for a local installation, but the container's .opencodex directory is image-owned and replaceable while only the OAuth directory is host-mounted. Relying on the generated file would change the administrator credential after replacement. The original runtime already supports an explicit environment token and rejects any collision with data-plane credentials.

retained: Independent management and data-plane admission domains
lost: Automatic local token-file generation is intentionally replaced by an orchestrator-provided production secret
parityAudit.decision: Require the original environment-supported management credential in both Compose variants and verify it through the unchanged management API.

components.functionality: Identity-aware production ingress smoke covering both services, dependency readiness, compiled GUI, security headers and anonymous admission
components.incompatibility: OpenCodex's liveness module discovers one local process from PID and runtime-port records. The production gate runs outside the containers and must verify two identities through an Nginx prefix plus readiness, static delivery and unauthenticated rejection; local PID discovery is unavailable and unnecessary at this boundary.

lost: PID and runtime-port discovery remain covered by the complete imported OpenCodex test suite
parityAudit.decision: Preserve the identity-first health invariant and extend it across the externally observable product topology.

components.functionality: Linux CI build, health-ordered startup, ingress smoke, failure logs and deterministic teardown of the production containers
components.incompatibility: 9router's workflow builds and publishes one multi-architecture image only for releases. AIWrapper needs a non-publishing pull-request gate that builds two local images, starts three health-dependent services, executes the same-origin product smoke and always removes volumes.

lost: Registry login, multi-architecture publication and release tags are intentionally outside the validation workflow
parityAudit.decision: Reuse the upstream Docker CI foundation for a fail-closed topology gate and keep image publication as a separate future release decision.

components.functionality: Cross-platform LF-canonical SHA-256 evidence for text checked out with Windows CRLF or Git LF
components.incompatibility: The upstream vendor manifest hashes raw bytes inside one package. AIWrapper's evidence is generated on Windows with core.autocrlf and verified on Linux CI, so raw hashes describe checkout-specific CRLF bytes rather than the canonical LF bytes committed by Git. Keeping raw hashing makes valid evidence unverifiable on another operating system.

lost: Checkout-specific CRLF is intentionally treated as the same textual artifact as committed LF
parityAudit.decision: Normalize only CRLF to LF before hashing; preserve all other bytes, including lone carriage returns, and use the helper symmetrically in generation and verification.

components.functionality: Pairwise and component-aggregate source/destination provenance manifest, metrics, evidence report and unified diff generation
components.incompatibility: The upstream generator verifies vendored SHA-256 values but does not compare arbitrary origin/destination pairs or emit line metrics and unified diffs required by AIWrapper.

retained: Bounded transient-write retry for Windows indexers
Git-index-closed directory expansion that excludes machine-local ignored files and retains tracked nested vendor artifacts
parityAudit.decision: The upstream manifest architecture is preserved and extended with required pairwise evidence, component-level aggregate metrics, canonical text hashing, Git-index-closed traversal and direct links to every unified diff rather than replaced.

components.functionality: Fail-closed verification of hashes, classifications, diffs and parity audits
components.incompatibility: The upstream verifier has no AIWrapper literal classification, pairwise diff integrity or mandatory own-code incompatibility checks.

retained: Symmetric LF-canonical source, destination and diff verification
Mandatory Git tracking for every source, destination and stored diff
parityAudit.decision: Upstream verification behavior is retained and strengthened for the acceptance policy.
